papers.title: Ban bets on unfinished clinical trials | Science
papers.summary: In July, the prediction market platform Kalshi and data company AppliedXL began a pilot market listing binary, yes-or-no contracts on whether named late-stage clinical trials meet their preregistered primary end points. Kalshi lists contracts only after trial enrollment closes, reasoning that a visible price—in effect the market’s odds that the trial succeeds—could sway recruitment. But closing enrollment does not end an experiment. Traders can buy and sell contracts while trial participants still attend visits, staff still measure outcomes, and interim results remain confidential. The line belongs at the end of the experiment, not of enrollment: No public contract on a trial’s efficacy or safety result should trade while the trial is ongoing and before the result is public

papers.title: BriGHT: transcriptome-regularized multimodal neuroimaging for brain disorder prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Hypergraph-based models for brain disorder prediction mainly adopt imaging-derived hypergraphs as propagation backbones. However, the entanglement of topology construction and feature propagation leaves regional representations weakly constrained by underlying biological organization, making them vulnerable to subject-specific variation and noise, particularly in heterogeneous multimodal settings. Results We present BriGHT, a B rain t r anscr i ptome-re G ularized H ypergraph framework for mul T imodal disorder prediction. BriGHT employs a transcriptome-derived structural reference as a soft anchoring prior to regularize neuroimaging ROI embeddings, stabilizing representation geometry while preserving disease-relevant subject-specific variation. BriGHT further incorporates a reliability-aware fusion module to estimate subject-specific modality reliability from prediction confidence, cross-modal consistency, and decision certainty, enabling adaptive integration under heterogeneous modality quality. Experiments on three neuroimaging cohorts (ADNI, ADHD-200, REST-meta-MDD) and four modalities (VBM, fMRI, FDG, AV45) demonstrate that BriGHT consistently outperforms competing graph/hypergraph learning methods across six brain disorder prediction tasks. Perturbation analyses show that BriGHT benefits from the spatial correspondence between transcriptomic modules and imaging ROIs, rather than from arbitrary hypergraph regularization alone. Ablation and meta-analytic interpretability analyses support the contribution of transcriptomic anchoring and adaptive fusion to robust and biologically meaningful brain disorder prediction. Availability The software is publicly available at: https://github.com/Yaolab-fantastic/BriGHT

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 摘要动机：用于脑部疾病预测的基于超图模型的方法，主要采用从影像数据中提取的超图作为信息传播的核心结构。
llm_highlights_zh: 然而，拓扑结构的构建与特征传播之间的紧密关联导致这些区域表征在很大程度上缺乏来自生物学组织的有效约束，因此它们极易受到特定研究对象的影响以及各种噪声的干扰，尤其是在异构的多模态环境中。

BriGHT利用从转录组数据中获得的结构参考信息作为“软锚点”，在规范化神经影像学感兴趣区域的嵌入表示时使用这一参考信息，从而在保持与疾病相关的个体差异的同时，稳定这些表示对象的几何结构。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
目前用于脑部疾病预测的基于超图模型的方法主要采用从影像数据中提取的超图作为信息传播的核心结构。然而，由于拓扑构建过程与特征传播机制之间存在紧密关联，这些模型所生成的区域表征在很大程度上缺乏生物学组织的约束，因此容易受到个体差异及噪声的影响，尤其是在异构多模态环境下。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了BriGHT这一基于转录组信息的超图框架，专门用于多模态脑部疾病预测。该框架首先利用转录组数据构建结构参考模型，作为对神经影像学数据嵌入结果的软性约束机制，从而在保持疾病相关特征的同时稳定表征结构；同时，它还整合了可靠性评估模块，通过分析预测置信度、跨模态一致性及决策确定性等因素来量化不同模态数据的可靠性，进而实现在不同质量的数据下的自适应融合。  

在三个神经影像学数据集（ADNI、ADHD-200、REST-meta-MDD）以及四种成像模式（VBM、fMRI、FDG、AV45）上进行的实验表明，BriGHT在六项脑部疾病预测任务中均显著优于其他同类模型。进一步分析发现，其优势主要源于转录组模块与影像学数据区域之间的空间对应关系，而非单纯的超图结构规范化处理。此外，消融实验及元分析结果也证实了转录组信息锚定机制与自适应融合策略对提升预测模型的鲁棒性与生物学解释性的重要性。  

**软件可用性**  
该软件已公开发布，访问地址为：https://github.com/Yaolab-fantastic/BriGHT

papers.title: A Novel Causality-Based Method for Identifying Drivers of Breast Cancer Progression
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Identifying transcriptomic factors with potential causal effects on breast cancer progression is important for understanding disease mechanisms and prioritizing therapeutic targets. However, causal-effect estimation from high-dimensional gene-expression data remains challenging because of the large number of variables and potential unmeasured confounding. Results We propose CICIV, a causal inference framework that integrates PC-simple-based causal feature selection with conditional instrumental variable (CIV) representation learning. PC-simple first reduces the dimensionality of transcriptomic data by identifying candidate parent genes, after which CIV estimates and ranks their absolute causal effects. Applied to TCGA-BRCA, CICIV prioritized 40 breast cancer-related candidate genes and identified signals that were not captured by conventional correlation-based analyses. External validation using the independent METABRIC cohort showed consistent effect directions for 21 of the 40 genes, with four genes overlapping in the Top 10 and nine in the Top 20 rankings. Pathway enrichment and literature-based analyses further supported the biological relevance of the prioritized genes. Availability and Implementation The CICIV benchmarking framework and source code are freely available at https://github.com/Zaiwen/CICIV . **摘要与动机**

**研究方法**

However, causal-effect estimation from high-dimensional gene-expression data remains challenging because of the large number of variables and potential unmeasured confounding. all_papers.title: Ban bets on unfinished clinical trials | Science
all_papers.summary: In July, the prediction market platform Kalshi and data company AppliedXL began a pilot market listing binary, yes-or-no contracts on whether named late-stage clinical trials meet their preregistered primary end points. Kalshi lists contracts only after trial enrollment closes, reasoning that a visible price—in effect the market’s odds that the trial succeeds—could sway recruitment. But closing enrollment does not end an experiment. Traders can buy and sell contracts while trial participants still attend visits, staff still measure outcomes, and interim results remain confidential. The line belongs at the end of the experiment, not of enrollment: No public contract on a trial’s efficacy or safety result should trade while the trial is ongoing and before the result is public

llm_highlights_zh: Kalshi仅在试验招募结束之后才会公布相关合同条款，她认为，一个明确的定价——实际上就是市场对于该试验能否成功的预期概率——可能会影响招募结果。
但是，停止招生并不意味着这项实验就此结束。
在试验参与者仍在接受随访、工作人员仍在测量各项指标、且中期结果尚未公开的情况下，交易者仍然可以买卖这些合约。

all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Hypergraph-based models for brain disorder prediction mainly adopt imaging-derived hypergraphs as propagation backbones. However, the entanglement of topology construction and feature propagation leaves regional representations weakly constrained by underlying biological organization, making them vulnerable to subject-specific variation and noise, particularly in heterogeneous multimodal settings. Results We present BriGHT, a B rain t r anscr i ptome-re G ularized H ypergraph framework for mul T imodal disorder prediction. BriGHT employs a transcriptome-derived structural reference as a soft anchoring prior to regularize neuroimaging ROI embeddings, stabilizing representation geometry while preserving disease-relevant subject-specific variation. BriGHT further incorporates a reliability-aware fusion module to estimate subject-specific modality reliability from prediction confidence, cross-modal consistency, and decision certainty, enabling adaptive integration under heterogeneous modality quality. Experiments on three neuroimaging cohorts (ADNI, ADHD-200, REST-meta-MDD) and four modalities (VBM, fMRI, FDG, AV45) demonstrate that BriGHT consistently outperforms competing graph/hypergraph learning methods across six brain disorder prediction tasks. Perturbation analyses show that BriGHT benefits from the spatial correspondence between transcriptomic modules and imaging ROIs, rather than from arbitrary hypergraph regularization alone. Ablation and meta-analytic interpretability analyses support the contribution of transcriptomic anchoring and adaptive fusion to robust and biologically meaningful brain disorder prediction. Availability The software is publicly available at: https://github.com/Yaolab-fantastic/BriGHT

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
目前用于脑部疾病预测的基于超图模型的方法主要采用从影像数据中提取的超图作为信息传播的核心结构。然而，由于拓扑构建过程与特征传播机制之间存在紧密关联，这些模型所生成的区域表征在很大程度上缺乏生物学组织的约束，因此容易受到个体差异及噪声的影响，尤其是在异构多模态环境下。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了BriGHT这一基于转录组信息的超图框架，专门用于多模态脑部疾病预测。该框架首先利用转录组数据构建结构参考模型，作为对神经影像学数据嵌入结果的软性约束机制，从而在保持疾病相关特征的同时稳定表征结构；同时，它还整合了可靠性评估模块，通过分析预测置信度、跨模态一致性及决策确定性等因素来量化不同模态数据的可靠性，进而实现在不同质量的数据下的自适应融合。  

在三个神经影像学数据集（ADNI、ADHD-200、REST-meta-MDD）以及四种成像模式（VBM、fMRI、FDG、AV45）上进行的实验表明，BriGHT在六项脑部疾病预测任务中均显著优于其他同类模型。进一步分析发现，其优势主要源于转录组模块与影像学数据区域之间的空间对应关系，而非单纯的超图结构规范化处理。此外，消融实验及元分析结果也证实了转录组信息锚定机制与自适应融合策略对提升预测模型的鲁棒性与生物学解释性的重要性。  

**软件可用性**  
该软件已公开发布，访问地址为：https://github.com/Yaolab-fantastic/BriGHT

all_papers.title: A Novel Causality-Based Method for Identifying Drivers of Breast Cancer Progression
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Identifying transcriptomic factors with potential causal effects on breast cancer progression is important for understanding disease mechanisms and prioritizing therapeutic targets. However, causal-effect estimation from high-dimensional gene-expression data remains challenging because of the large number of variables and potential unmeasured confounding. Results We propose CICIV, a causal inference framework that integrates PC-simple-based causal feature selection with conditional instrumental variable (CIV) representation learning. PC-simple first reduces the dimensionality of transcriptomic data by identifying candidate parent genes, after which CIV estimates and ranks their absolute causal effects. Applied to TCGA-BRCA, CICIV prioritized 40 breast cancer-related candidate genes and identified signals that were not captured by conventional correlation-based analyses. External validation using the independent METABRIC cohort showed consistent effect directions for 21 of the 40 genes, with four genes overlapping in the Top 10 and nine in the Top 20 rankings. Pathway enrichment and literature-based analyses further supported the biological relevance of the prioritized genes.
